item.text:
You were right, and the false positive was worse than a threshold problem — it was a lie about what the watchdog had actually read.

## The bug

`thr_v9cx8hmnw5` has ~11,300 events. On first sight I paged its log **forwards from seq 0, 100 events a pass**, so the cursor spent about an hour in yesterday evening. Meanwhile `long_turn` measured `now − turnStartedMs`, and `turnStartedMs` was a turn that opened 16 hours ago and closed 15 hours ago — its `turn/completed` sat at seq 500, past the page the watchdog had reached.

```
seq1   turn/started    09-19 19:59:45   ← folded
seq2..499  …            (turn/completed at seq 500 never reached)
reported: severe — "Turn has run 57969s with no result"
actual:   active, last event 16s ago, working fine
```

So it wasn't flagging a stuck thread. It was reporting the age of its own cursor.

## The fix

- **First sight reads backwards from the newest event.** A watchdog watches the present; it doesn't audit history.
- Later pages move forward only, and a pass drains up to five pages before admitting it is behind.
- **`stall` and `long_turn` are withheld until the reading is at the head of the log.** Those two measure wall clock, and wall clock against a stale cursor is meaningless. `loop`, `context_cliff`, `budget`, and `error_storm` keep firing — they're proved by the events already in hand.

Regression test replays the real paging contract (`afterSeq` / `order` / `limit`) over an 1,200-event thread and asserts the phantom finding cannot come back. 45 tests green, shipped as **0.1.1**, committed.

## What that thread actually looks like now

```
$ bb shepherd explain thr_v9cx8hmnw5
thr_v9cx8hmnw5: status active, last event 16s ago, 24 recent steps
  warn context_cliff: Context 95% full (244731/258400 tokens)
```

The severe long turn is gone, and the same thread now reports something true and worth having: it is at **95% of its context window** and about to fall off it. That's the finding that was hiding behind the fake one.

## The cost, stated plainly

A turn that opened more than one page ago has no start in the head window, so `long_turn` waits for the next turn instead of guessing. I took that trade deliberately — a missed long turn is recoverable, a fabricated one teaches you to ignore the panel.

Two things you should know about how I got here: I shipped the cursor design without ever testing a thread with real history, and my earlier `error_storm` count was inflated 3× for the same class of reason (one failed turn arriving through three different keys). Both were caught by pointing it at your actual fleet rather than my fixtures. It's in `off` mode, so nothing was ever sent to that thread on the strength of the bad reading.
